metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (real corpus + testdata evidence of terminal:"failed"); daemon_capability: full, but the reached final state is `error`, not the scenario's literal `ready` — muse's SessionError mechanism routes every detected model-call failure to a persistent error state rather than a silent recovery, which is the correct/more-informative behavior (see body); driver_capability: gap:base_url_override (launch_repl() does not yet wire settings into the muse invocation). OBSERVABILITY_CORRECTION (2026-09-14, record phase): daemon_capability corrected full -> bug. base_url_override was ported (driver-interactive.sh's spawn_muse_repl) and the induced failure itself works exactly as assessed -- confirmed live, twice: terminal:"failed", reason="transport error...(after 4 provider attempts)", turn_duration_ms~2015. But the scenario's own defining assertion (session reaches error and stays there) could NOT be observed through the daemon on either live attempt: both show the SAME pre-existing post-birth-transcript-churn bug (#1960 onboarding brief) deterministically (not racy, unlike its manifestation in session-end) -- transcript_removed fires ~0.26-0.72s after birth with no re-discovery, and the real session's working/error classification never fires for the rest of its ~8s life despite the daemon correctly tailing 169KB+ of real transcript_activity for it the whole time. process_exited also misattributes to the session's own proc-<PID> presession shadow (the same processlifecycle watched-map last-write-wins bug that hit session-end). Both are the SAME two pre-identified daemon bugs, not new ones -- no issue filed. driver_capability corrected gap:base_url_override -> ready (the launch-arg wiring itself works; the daemon-side observation is what fails). OBSERVABILITY_CORRECTION #2 (2026-09-14, record phase, recording 2026-09-14-06-40-20_irrlichd-0.6.3+9abf13d, git_head=9abf13d1): daemon_capability corrected bug -> full. Re-recorded after landing commit 9abf13d1 ("fix(daemon): never let a proc-* pre-session evict a real session's PID claim", core/application/services/pid_manager.go), which stops assignPIDLocked's same-PID stale-holder scan from deleting the real session in favor of a late-arriving proc-* presession claim. On this third live attempt the real session is never evicted -- no transcript_removed fires for it at all -- and it cleanly transitions ready->working->error via the session_error classifier rule, staying in error for the rest of its life. turn_start and turn_failed, previously KNOWN_FAILING, now pass and are corrected in expected.jsonl. The scenario's own defining assertion (session reaches error and stays there) is therefore observed correctly, matching the original assessment's daemon_capability=full verdict. A SEPARATE, unrelated daemon bug remains: process_exited for the real session is still misattributed to its transient proc-<PID> presession (processlifecycle's watched map[int]string last-write-wins, same shape as session-end) -- not touched by 9abf13d1, not newly discovered. known_failing stays true, now scoped to the teardown phase only (see expected.jsonl).

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full (final state is `error`, not the scenario's literal `ready` — see "Why the final state is `error`, not `ready`" below)
driver_capability: gap:base_url_override
route: driver-gap

## Reasoning

### agent = yes

Muse's own runtime detects and terminally reports a model-call failure mid-turn. Every prompt opens a `run` with `payload_type:"runtime.session", payload.kind:"run", event.kind:"started"` and closes with `event.kind:"terminal"`, whose `terminal` field discriminates the outcome (format-spec §3; parser.go comment cites 37 samples across the 14-session corpus: 31 `completed`, ~5-6 `cancelled` variants, 1 `failed`). TWO independent, structurally different `terminal:"failed"` examples exist on this machine:

1. **Real production sample** (format-spec §3/§11, live-captured, not synthesized): `reason:"model stream idle timeout after 30000ms"` — a genuine mid-stream network/provider stall, no preceding `run_fatal_error_classified` event (the parser's fallback path, `class="terminal_failed"`).
2. **`testdata/real-turn-failed.jsonl`** (committed adapter fixture): `event.kind:"run_fatal_error_classified","error_class":"config_error"` immediately followed by `terminal:"failed","reason":"invalid run configuration: provider does not support base instructions"`.

Both are handled by the SAME code path (`parser.go` `parseRunTerminal`, case `terminalFailed`) and are directly unit-tested: `TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Failed_UsesPrecedingErrorClass` (the config_error shape) and `TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Failed_FallsBackWithNoErrorClass` (the idle-timeout shape, no preceding classifier event) — both green under `go test ./core/... -race -count=1` (verified green by exit code per this task's brief). That two structurally unrelated failure classes (a pure network stall vs. a config validation error) both funnel through the identical `terminal:"failed"` → `run_fatal_error_classified`-or-fallback shape is strong evidence this is muse's GENERAL failure-reporting mechanism, not a narrow special case.

### daemon = full

`parseRunTerminal` sets `EventType="turn_done"` for every terminal outcome (the run objectively ends in all cases) AND, on `terminalFailed`, sets `ev.SessionError` (`Phase: ErrorPhaseUnknown, Class: <error_class or "terminal_failed">, Message: <reason>`). `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`'s `session_error` rule (`id: string(session.SignalSessionError)`, ~line 283) fires whenever `m.SessionError != nil && !m.HookTurnDone` and decides `session.StateError` directly — this rule sits ABOVE `classifyAgentDone` in the authority ladder, and muse declares no hooks (agent.go's doc comment: "the adapter is observe-only ... no hooks"), so `HookTurnDone` is always false for muse and this rule fires unconditionally the instant `SessionError` is set. Even if that rule were somehow bypassed, `classifyAgentDone` itself independently checks `metrics.SessionError != nil` and returns `StateError` too (line ~433-434) — the daemon has two independent, converging paths to the same correct outcome. `SessionError` clears only when the user starts a fresh turn (`clearSessionErrorOnRecovery`, gated on a new `started`/`user_message` event) — it is not cleared by the failing turn's own epilogue.

The session therefore never sticks in `working` (resolution is immediate and event-driven — no inactivity sweep is needed at all, unlike several sibling agents' 2.14 cells that rely on IdleFlush/staleWorking backstops), and it resolves to a state that accurately, persistently signals the failure to the user.

### Why the final state is `error`, not `ready` — the scenario's literal wording does not fit muse, and that is a feature, not a gap

Scenario 2.14's acceptance_criteria (as written, generically across the fleet) says "State topology: ready → working → ready" / "Final state: ready", reflecting agents whose failure-recovery is either silent (no persisted signal at all) or resolves via an ordinary `turn_done`-shaped epilogue that the classifier treats the same as a normal completion (this is exactly what every OTHER onboarded agent's 2.14 cell shows — claudecode/copilot/gemini-cli/opencode/pi/aider all settle back to `ready`; none reaches `error`, checked directly against their committed expected.jsonl files in this repo).

Muse is architecturally different: its `terminal:"failed"` event is a DISTINCT, self-classified outcome from `terminal:"completed"`, and the adapter deliberately keeps `SessionError` strictly separate from an ordinary tool `IsError` (parser.go's own comment on this: "set `SessionError` on a genuine session-level failure ... never on an ordinary tool failure"). Both real-world failure samples in the corpus (idle-timeout and config_error) took this path, and NEITHER corpus nor the format-spec's research turned up any example or documented mechanism by which muse recovers SILENTLY from a failed model call with no `terminal:"failed"`/`SessionError` trace at all (the scenario's own "Bucket B" — a pure network drop with zero transcript write — is not observed for muse; every failure the corpus captured produced a `terminal` event of some kind). So there is no evidence muse exhibits the "silently recovers to ready" shape 2.14 describes at all; what it reliably exhibits instead is the "session goes red and stays red until the user's next turn" shape that scenarios 2.22/2.23/2.24 exist specifically to test (2.23 `provider-overloaded-terminal` and 2.24 `auth-credentials-rejected` both assert `ready → working → error`, `Final state: error`, checked directly — their committed expected.jsonl for claudecode asserts exactly this topology for what is architecturally the identical underlying event: a provider call fails, the agent gives up, the daemon paints the session red and keeps it there).

Per the caveats-over-downgrades rule, I considered downgrading this to `daemon=bug` (the daemon "gets the wrong state") or leaving the spec asserting `ready` (matching the scenario's literal words) and marking the cell `known_failing`. I rejected both: nothing is mishandled here — the daemon is accurately reporting a real, ongoing failure condition, and forcing a silent return to `ready` would be the actual defect (this is exactly the "silent-green" failure mode 2.23's own description calls out as the thing #1796 exists to prevent). I judged `daemon_capability: full` and wrote `expected.jsonl` to assert muse's real, correct arc (`ready → working → error`) rather than a literal but wrong `ready`, and I am flagging this deviation prominently here (not just in a caveat) because it is a genuine, evidence-based departure from the scenario's stated acceptance criteria, not a narrow detail.

### driver = gap:base_url_override

`muse --help` (run directly on this machine) documents `--base-url <URL>` — "Override the Meta provider base URL" — a deterministic, zero-API-cost way to force every model call to fail: point it at a local port nothing listens on (mirrors copilot's proven `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`-at-a-dead-port pattern for this exact scenario, and claudecode's `mock-anthropic-5xx` pattern; both are committed precedent in this repo for 2.14). The recipe's own step SEQUENCE needs nothing new — `send` / `wait_turn` / `sleep` / `exit_clean` are all already in `driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS`. The gap is that `launch_repl()` (replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh) hardcodes its launch command to `tmux new-session ... "muse" --trust-workspace` and explicitly does NOT read `$SETTINGS_PATH` into the launch invocation — the driver's own comment on that positional argument says so directly: "SETTINGS_PATH ... though this adapter's launch does not read it." So a recipe `settings.base_url` value has nowhere to land today. `record` must extend `launch_repl()` to read `base_url` (and any future launch-time override) out of `$SETTINGS_PATH` and append `--base-url "$value"` to the muse invocation before driving — a launch-argument wiring gap, not a missing step-type primitive, hence `gap:base_url_override` rather than one of the standard `keys`/`interrupt`/etc. primitives.
caveats: UNVERIFIED: whether an immediate TCP connection refusal (a closed local port) produces the SAME terminal:"failed" shape as the two captured samples. The idle-timeout sample implies a connection that succeeded but then stalled (~30s), and the config_error sample never attempted a network call at all — neither is a direct precedent for an immediate ECONNREFUSED. This is a reasonable inference from muse's general run_fatal_error_classified→terminal:failed catch-all shape (two unrelated failure classes already funnel through it), not a confirmed third example. `record` should confirm the captured reason/error_class names a connection/network failure and use observability_correction if the daemon-observable shape differs from what's asserted here.

Vacuous-pass check: this cell would pass while proving nothing if the recording environment lacks any configured muse provider credential (muse login / META_API_KEY) and muse rejects the run for missing auth BEFORE ever consulting --base-url — the induced failure would then be a credentials/config gate, not a genuine mid-turn model-call failure, though it would still exercise the identical SessionError→error daemon path. `record` must confirm muse has SOME credential configured (same out-of-band precondition 2-1/2-13 already carry) and that the captured failure text names a connection problem, not an auth-configuration one.

Session-birth shape (single birth vs. a transient proc-<PID> pre-session minted by the daemon's unconditional per-adapter process scanner, wiring.go:103) is NOT live-confirmed for muse — no muse recording exists in this repo yet. This is the identical open question 2-13_turn-end-terminal-text's assessment already flagged (citing the same wiring.go code); I've written phases the same defensive way (pi-pattern: session_birth unpinned to any session, turn_start anchored to start and also unpinned so it matches whichever session first goes working, every later phase pinned via same_session_as) for the same reason and consistency with that sibling cell.

terminal:"cancelled"'s status as a genuine human-ESC signal vs. programmatic cancellation is UNVERIFIED (format-spec §3/§12) but irrelevant to this cell, which only exercises terminal:"failed" — noted since parseRunTerminal's cancelled branch is adjacent, untouched code.

Whether muse ever auto-retries a failed run without a fresh "started" event in between is UNVERIFIED (parser.go's own comment) — irrelevant to this cell's single-turn recipe (SessionError clearing depends on this only across MULTIPLE turns), but would matter for a retry-ladder variant.

cost_nonzero/tokens_nonzero asserted false: neither captured failed-turn sample contains a model_completed event (the config_error sample fails before any model call; the idle-timeout sample never receives a response to account usage from), so Contribution/Tokens should stay nil for the aborted turn. model is left unpinned/empty for the same reason: ModelName is set from model_completed/run_model_configured/model_reconfigure records that were not present before failure in the one fixture I can inspect line-by-line (real-turn-failed.jsonl); record should fill in whatever the live daemon actually reports.

Absence-of-evidence claim, marked as such: no example of the scenario's own "Bucket B" (a pure network drop with literally zero transcript write, leaving the session stuck in working with no daemon signal at all) was found anywhere in the 14-session corpus or in the format-spec/adapter-contract research, and muse's run_fatal_error_classified→terminal:failed mechanism looks designed to be a catch-all for exactly this class of failure — but this is inferred from the absence of a counter-example, not a confirmed guarantee that no such silent-failure path exists in muse.

RECORD-TIME OBSERVABILITY_CORRECTION: daemon_capability full->bug, live-confirmed twice (both attempts identical). See metadata.notes for the full account. Not a new daemon bug -- both of the two pre-identified ones (#1960 brief), reproduced deterministically here rather than racily.

RECORD-TIME OBSERVABILITY_CORRECTION #2 (2026-09-14, recording 2026-09-14-06-40-20_irrlichd-0.6.3+9abf13d): daemon_capability bug->full after commit 9abf13d1 fixed the proc-* PID-claim eviction bug. Live-confirmed on a third attempt: the real session is never evicted, and ready->working->error is now observed cleanly and stays put. Only the teardown phase (process_exited misattribution, a separate pre-existing bug) remains known_failing -- see expected.jsonl meta notes for the full account.

sources.note: parseRunTerminal (~line 317-365): terminalFailed sets EventType=turn_done + SessionError{Phase:ErrorPhaseUnknown, Class, Message}; terminalCompleted/terminalCancelled do not set SessionError. lastErrorClass mechanism (parseRunFatalErrorClassified, ~line 516-522) captures the preceding run_fatal_error_classified's error_class for the terminal record to consume.

TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Failed_UsesPrecedingErrorClass and TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Failed_FallsBackWithNoErrorClass cover both real captured failure shapes end-to-end; TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Cancelled_NoErrorNoInterruptFlag confirms cancelled is deliberately NOT a SessionError.

Committed real fixture: started -> resource_usage_sampled -> run_fatal_error_classified{error_class:config_error} -> terminal{failed, reason:"invalid run configuration: provider does not support base instructions"}.

session_error rule (~line 283-288, signal: session.SignalSessionError, fires when SessionError!=nil && !HookTurnDone) decides StateError directly, above classifyAgentDone in the ladder; classifyAgentDone (~line 396-452) independently also routes SessionError!=nil to StateError as a second, converging path.
applySessionError/clearSessionErrorOnRecovery: SessionError is sticky across passes and clears only when the user starts a fresh turn, not on the failing turn's own epilogue.

Sibling scenario, same underlying event class (provider call fails, agent gives up) asserting ready->working->error, Final state: error — direct precedent that this daemon-observable shape is a recognized, intentional pattern in this matrix, not a defect.
Second sibling precedent for the same ready->working->error, Final state: error shape.

Every other onboarded agent's 2.14 cell (copilot/gemini-cli/opencode/pi/aider/claudecode, checked directly) settles back to ready, not error -- confirms muse's error-ending arc is a genuine, evidence-based departure specific to muse's architecture, not a copy-paste mistake.

Sibling muse assessment (same classifier mechanism, terminal:completed case) already flags the identical unresolved session-birth-shape question, citing wiring.go's unconditional per-adapter process scanner; I aligned this cell's phase-anchoring with that one for consistency.

buildAgentWatchers (~line 40-103): a processlifecycle.Scanner is constructed unconditionally for every adapter regardless of Source variant, confirming a muse proc-<PID> pre-session is plausible even though muse is FilesUnderRoot.

launch_repl() hardcodes `tmux new-session ... "muse" --trust-workspace`; the SETTINGS_PATH positional argument's own comment states the launch does not read it. DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean" covers every step type this recipe's script needs.
turn_count() matches any event.kind=="terminal" record regardless of the terminal field's value, so wait_turn correctly unblocks on a failed run, not only a completed one.

sources.ref: muse --help (run live on this machine, muse-bin 1.2.1-R2847.1)
sources.note: Documents --base-url <URL> ("Override the Meta provider base URL") and --model <MODEL>, confirming the deterministic elicitation mechanism this recipe relies on.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1)

muse auth complete (muse login, or META_API_KEY exported) -- same out-of-band precondition as muse/2-1_basic-turn and muse/2-13_turn-end-terminal-text; must be confirmed present so the induced failure is a genuine connection failure, not a masked auth-configuration gate (see caveats)
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL so the process survives the aborted turn and can still receive /exit
irrlichd is recording (either run-cell.sh isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record)

DRIVER GAP (record must close before this cell can run): replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl() must be extended to read a base_url key out of $SETTINGS_PATH and append `--base-url "$value"` to the muse launch invocation -- today that file is read but ignored (see driver_capability: gap:base_url_override)
a local TCP port with nothing listening on it at record time (e.g. 18799, matching the copilot 2-14 precedent's dead-port pattern) for --base-url to point at
setup: Same launch shape as muse/2-1_basic-turn: a fresh empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/, `muse --trust-workspace --base-url http://127.0.0.1:<dead-port>` in a tmux session, 1s settle sleep before the first send (both live-reproduced necessities per muse-driver-audit.md).

The prompt content does not matter for cue-avoidance the way it does in other cells: the model call fails before any assistant text is ever generated, so there is no risk of a waiting-cue false match. Keep it simple, e.g. "Say hello."
wait_turn's turn_count() matches any event.kind=="terminal" record (turn-count.sh), so it correctly unblocks as soon as the failed run's own terminal event lands -- no special-casing needed there.
verify: events.jsonl mints a session in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishes launching
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event binding the muse-bin PID to the real session
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working when the user prompt lands (event.kind:"started" -> user_message)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to error after the model call fails (event.kind:"terminal",terminal:"failed" -> SessionError -> session_error classifier rule)
the session does NOT stick in working, and does NOT re-enter ready or waiting after the failure
final session state is error before exit_clean tears the REPL down (error is sticky -- it clears only on the user's next turn, which this recipe never sends)
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=false, cost_nonzero=false (no model_completed event before the failure), model unpinned
